title: Insecure Storage and Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys
platform_conditions: Android runtime (API level 1+ for SharedPreferences; the AndroidKeyStore provider exists from API 18)
security_mechanism: SharedPreferences writes a plaintext XML file in the app sandbox; on rooted devices, in backups (android:allowBackup), and through any sandbox escape the file is readable, so auth tokens and keys stored there are recoverable offline. Keys compiled into the app ship in the APK/dex and are extracted with static analysis by anyone who downloads it, so 'encrypted with a hardcoded key' is only obfuscation. Cipher.getInstance("AES") without a transformation returns AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding, which encrypts equal plaintext blocks to equal ciphertext and leaks structure; keys generated outside the AndroidKeyStore provider stay extractable from the filesystem.

source_sink_clues.source: The stored material itself: session tokens, refresh tokens, user data, and keys/constants embedded in the app binary.
source_sink_clues.sink: prefs.edit().putString("token", ...) for secrets; hardcoded key strings/byte arrays passed to SecretKeySpec; Cipher.getInstance("AES") or any ECB transformation; writes to external storage

tracking_guards: Check secrets live in the Android Keystore (AndroidKeyStore provider, KeyGenParameterSpec with ENCRYPT_MODE purposes) or in EncryptedSharedPreferences/AndroidX security-crypto backed by it, not in plain SharedPreferences; check no key material appears as a string or literals in the source/APK; check Cipher.getInstance names a full transformation with GCM or CBC + random IV and MAC; check android:allowBackup="false" or backup rules exclude the secrets store.
not_candidate_when: The stored value is non-sensitive (UI prefs, cache), the key is generated inside AndroidKeyStore and never leaves secure hardware, or the cipher is fully specified (AES/GCM/NoPadding) with keys from the Keystore and the only plaintext values are non-secret.
public_references: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html
Android developer documentation: Android Keystore system — https://developer.android.com/training/articles/keystore.html
